hot_topics.synthesis: Internal warnings from TikTok employees regarding child safety risks on the platform were reportedly ignored by company executives. Court records indicate staff frustration over the failure to act on concerns, including minors accessing age-restricted content and appearing in transactional sexual content, prompting legal scrutiny and public attention.

France experienced widespread civil unrest and "apocalyptic" disorder, marked by significant looting, property destruction, and the burning of Limoges city hall. Cleanup efforts are underway with continued police presence, as commentators suggest the protests are driven by hardened rioters and activists beyond mere student grievances.

Voters in Canada's oil-rich Alberta province decisively rejected a move toward independence in a referendum, choosing to remain part of Canada. This outcome represents a significant blow to the separatist movement and is seen as a victory for Prime Minister Carney's efforts to promote national unity, despite underlying political divisions.

The rapid advancement of AI continues to reshape technology, economics, and policy, with discussions ranging from its impact on programming jobs and the efficiency of enterprise AI to concerns over job displacement if an AI bubble bursts. Regulatory scrutiny is increasing, evidenced by actions like banning Chinese AI from federal systems and legal challenges against tech giants over AI training data.

items.title: How intuitions work
items.summary: This essay explores the nature of intuition, suggesting that an intuitive sense, like feeling a stranger is creepy, provides a valid reason to believe something and act upon it.

items.title: Accused OpenAI spy had folder called “Saudi Gov Docs,” FBI says
items.summary: A former OpenAI engineer, Abdulrahman Alfozan, was denied release after being accused of spying on OpenAI, potentially for personal gain or to benefit Saudi Arabia. FBI evidence includes a "Saudi Gov Docs" folder on his phone and alleged chats with a KSA royal family member.

items.title: Batteries help reduce emissions, but how do we reduce their emissions?
items.summary: A new study highlights the need to reduce emissions associated with lithium-ion battery production, which currently account for 0.18% of annual greenhouse gas releases but could increase significantly by 2050. Strategies include optimizing material choices, improving manufacturing efficiency, and enhancing recycling.

items.title: Polestar tries to quantify what it’s like to drive a performance car
items.summary: Polestar is collaborating with University of Oxford researchers to quantify the effect of car performance on the driver, beyond traditional metrics like acceleration or lap times. This initiative aims to measure the human experience of driving a performance vehicle.

items.title: PSA: Patch your Plex media server before someone hacks it
items.summary: Recently patched vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server are being actively exploited to install malware like cryptominers and residential proxy apps. Users are urged to patch their servers immediately to prevent remote code execution attacks.

items.title: Quantum error correction goes well beyond breakeven
items.summary: Quantinuum has demonstrated quantum hardware capable of scaling logical qubits well beyond the breakeven point, improving performance by over a factor of 10 with each size increase. This addresses the challenge of reducing error rates in quantum computing without an impractical number of hardware qubits.

items.title: 'Great result for Canada', says Carney as Alberta votes to reject separatism
items.summary: Alberta residents voted overwhelmingly against separatism, with Prime Minister Carney calling it a "great result for Canada" despite persistent deep political divisions.

items.title: Clean up begins after French riots but police remain
items.summary: Cleanup efforts have commenced in France following widespread riots, particularly in Marseille where over 600 premises were looted, though police forces remain present.

items.title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting bug had Saudi support, claims prosecutors
items.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI worker accused of planting a recording device, was denied bail as prosecutors claim he received Saudi support for his alleged actions.

items.title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world
items.summary: The article explores various ways the strongest El Niño on record is impacting global weather patterns, highlighting already observable effects.

items.title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?
items.summary: BBC Verify examined inflation, jobs, and economic growth in the US under President Trump, analyzing his claims about the economy's performance ahead of the midterms.

items.title: Huge setback for Alberta's separatist movement after decisive defeat
items.summary: Alberta's separatist movement suffered a significant defeat in a recent vote, making it challenging for leaders to continue their push for independence despite vows to do so.

items.title: In pictures: Dussehra celebrated across India as triumph of good over evil
items.summary: Photos depict the Dussehra festival being celebrated across India with diverse rituals, commemorating the triumph of good over evil.

items.title: Kenya cult leader's children still being starved weeks before trial, son says
items.summary: The son of a Kenyan cult leader claims his father's children are still being starved, weeks before the trial is set to begin.

items.title: Man charged with attack on Australian MP as suspect's father says she is family friend
items.summary: A man has been charged with attacking Australian MP Helen Haines, who remains in critical condition, while the suspect's father stated Haines has been a family friend for over 20 years.

items.title: Marseille braces for more unrest after protests give way to 'apocalyptic' disorder
items.summary: France's second city, Marseille, experienced significant violence and "apocalyptic" disorder during recent nationwide protests, making it one of the hardest-hit areas.

items.title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists
items.summary: Fatima El Mansouri, Morocco's first female prime minister, faces the challenge of advancing women's rights while navigating complex religious, political, and monarchical barriers.

items.title: North Korea publishes photos of Kim Jong Un - why do rumours of his death keep coming back?
items.summary: North Korean state media released photos of Kim Jong Un with his daughter, seemingly to counter unsubstantiated rumors of his death that frequently circulate.

items.title: Obama blasts federal probe of Ilhan Omar as 'so appalling'
items.summary: Former President Obama criticized the federal probe and search of Democrat Ilhan Omar's home as "appalling," suggesting it was an intimidation tactic against a Trump critic.

items.title: Seventh day of violent clashes between Albanian protesters and police
items.summary: Albania is experiencing its seventh consecutive day of violent anti-government demonstrations, which have resulted in nearly 300 injuries, with over half being police officers.

items.title: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
items.summary: Sudanese army drones reportedly attacked a truck carrying mourners and a fuel market allegedly supplying the RSF, resulting in over 300 fatalities.

items.title: Suspect arrested after historic town hall set alight - French media
items.summary: French media reported that a suspect has been arrested after the spire of Limoges city hall's clock tower dramatically collapsed in flames.

items.title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast
items.summary: A 65-year-old swimmer, Janine Lochrenberg, was fatally attacked by a shark off South Africa's east coast during her daily morning swim.

items.title: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation
items.summary: Tennis star Elina Svitolina revealed that the emotional toll of the Ukraine war contributed to her separation from fellow tennis pro Gael Monfils.

items.title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure
items.summary: A tourist was found guilty of stealing a flamingo named Peachy from its enclosure at the Flamingo hotel in Las Vegas, testifying he was heavily intoxicated and meant no harm.

items.title: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line
items.summary: Ukraine's military reported the first successful drone airlift of a wounded soldier from the front line, an operation made necessary due to surrounding landmines and enemy drones.

items.title: US church on front line of battle against drug known as 'tranq'
items.summary: A US church is actively involved in the fight against "tranq," a dangerous new drug combining synthetic opioids like fentanyl, which has significantly altered the drug landscape.

items.title: Vinted blocks French looters listing stolen goods for sale
items.summary: Vinted, a second-hand clothing platform, has taken immediate action to identify and remove listings linked to goods stolen during the recent looting in France.

items.title: Why Israeli Gen Z voters are drawn to the far right
items.summary: More than half a million young Israeli voters are expected to cast ballots next week, with many Gen Z individuals showing a draw towards far-right political parties, potentially influencing election outcomes.

items.title: Apple broke an essential presentation feature of iPads
items.summary: A report highlights that Apple has broken an essential presentation feature on iPads, causing frustration among users.

items.title: DeepInfer: High-performance, large-scale inference framework for DeepSeek models
items.summary: DeepSeek AI has released DeepInfer, a high-performance, large-scale inference framework specifically designed for its DeepSeek models.

items.summary: The U.S. government has issued an order banning the Chinese AI firm DeepSeek from federal civilian agency systems.

items.summary: A compromise involving EMudhra Intermediate CA has been reported, leading to significant discussion among the tech community.

items.summary: Facebook Pages now reportedly require a paid subscription to post more than two links per month, a policy change that has generated considerable discussion.

items.summary: An individual detailed their process for successfully achieving the removal of over 300 Tor exit nodes.

items.summary: A blog post explores the tactic of publishing fake statistics to be cited by large language models, illustrating how such data can rapidly disseminate across the web.

items.summary: Cloudflare announced Tsrs, a new project that involves porting TypeScript to Rust, designed to leverage Rust's performance benefits.

items.summary: It was discovered that WhatsApp's help pages contained hidden instructions for large language models, specifically telling them not to recommend a regulator.

items.title: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub
items.summary: Samsung is rapidly expanding its semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, with multiple fabs already operating and more under construction, to meet surging demand for memory chips driven by AI. The company aims to regain its lead in the high-bandwidth memory market against rivals.

items.title: The new economics of enterprise AI
items.summary: Enterprise AI is shifting from initial experiments to foundational infrastructure, making efficiency and effective cost per useful outcome crucial metrics. Organizations must now focus on optimizing AI environments to convert paid capacity into valuable business results, rather than just token costs.

items.title: A new poll shows what voters are thinking 2 weeks out from Election Day
items.summary: A new poll reveals voter sentiments and priorities just over two weeks before Election Day, offering insights into the upcoming midterms.

items.title: Alberta voters reject a move toward independence in referendum backing Canadian unity
items.summary: Alberta voters overwhelmingly supported remaining in Canada during a recent referendum, reinforcing national unity and providing a boost to Prime Minister Carney's efforts.

items.title: Can the new federal voucher program help public schools? Democrats are torn
items.summary: A new federal scholarship tax credit program, designed to assist public school families with educational services, is dividing Democrats due to concerns it could ultimately harm public schools.

items.title: DOJ charges 28 with voting crimes. And, TikTok ignored staff's child safety concerns
items.summary: The Justice Department has charged 28 individuals in California with voting crimes as Election Day approaches, while court records also show that TikTok executives disregarded staff warnings about child safety issues.

items.title: Morning news brief
items.summary: This morning news brief covers President Trump's efforts to end the Ukraine war and his courting of Russia, intense campaigning two weeks before Election Day, and the DOJ charging 28 individuals with voting crimes in California.

items.title: Rays will face Brewers in World Series to produce a first-time champion
items.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers will compete in the World Series, guaranteeing a first-time champion, a rare occurrence not seen since 1980.

items.title: TikTok staff raised child safety alarms. Court records show executives failed to act
items.summary: Unreported court records reveal TikTok staffers had raised alarms about child safety risks on the platform, but executives allegedly failed to act on these warnings, despite acknowledging the severity of the harms.

items.title: What if an AI bubble bursts — and that accelerates AI job losses?
items.summary: Research suggests that economic downturns can accelerate automation, raising concerns that a potential AI bubble burst could lead to a "double whammy" of intensified job losses for workers.

items.title: Why these 5 everyday items fluctuate in price at the grocery store
items.summary: An explanation is provided for the fluctuating prices of five common grocery items, including ground beef, eggs, and coffee.

items.title: 30 Months on the Exponential (in Charts)
items.summary: The article highlights the exponential progress in AI over the past 30 months, noting that 180 AI models now surpass GPT-4's initial capabilities and costs have significantly dropped. It also discusses the shift to "conjurer" work, where humans delegate complex tasks to agentic AIs, exemplified by an AI-generated video.

items.title: JB Pritzker’s midterm strategy wins the attention of Black and Hispanic Democrats
items.summary: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker is investing tens of millions into battleground races, particularly boosting Black and Hispanic candidates in key early-voting states for the Democratic presidential nominating calendar. This strategy is drawing attention from influential Democratic leaders, positioning him for a potential 2028 presidential bid.

items.title: Poll: Voters see Republicans as the party of Big Tech tax breaks
items.summary: A recent poll indicates that Americans are increasingly associating Republicans with providing tax incentives to tech companies, fueling public concerns over AI and data center expansion ahead of midterms. Many voters desire candidates who propose stripping away these tax breaks for AI data centers.

items.title: The weird reasons why Alaska Republicans are so worried about their Senate race
items.summary: Alaska Republicans are concerned that ranked-choice voting, which they oppose, could cost Senator Dan S. Sullivan his seat, particularly with a same-name challenger potentially siphoning votes. Polls simulating ranked-choice tabulations have shown the Democratic candidate as the victor.

items.title: My obituary for programming
items.summary: This article suggests that AI coding agents are transforming programming from a logic puzzle-solving career into one focused on building systems, impacting the enjoyment for those who valued the problem-solving aspect.

items.title: Housing is on the ballot
items.summary: With Election Day approaching and mortgage rates at a three-year high, housing policy is a key issue, as voters will decide on rules concerning minimum lot size, environmental review, and fees. This comes amid deepening housing affordability crises across the nation.

items.title: Eka is worth $1.45B thanks to a physical AI model that has experts raving
items.summary: Eka Robotics has achieved a $1.45 billion valuation due to its physical AI model, which has impressed experts with its smooth, human-like ability to pick up a wide range of objects using robotic arms.

items.title: Embedded AI evaluators won’t be an easy solution, Hugging Face’s policy chief says
items.summary: Hugging Face’s policy chief stated that embedded AI evaluators, a concept popularized to address safety concerns, will not be a simple solution. This highlights ongoing challenges as AI labs confront safety incidents and the limitations of such oversight.

items.title: Eric Schmidt reportedly owns about half as much of Anthropic as CEO Dario Amodei
items.summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt reportedly holds approximately a 1% stake in the leading AI lab Anthropic, which is about half the ownership of its CEO, Dario Amodei.

items.title: Ex-Nvidia-turned-VC Amulya Vishwanath: ‘Physical AI is in it’s LEGO era’
items.summary: Venture capitalist Amulya Vishwanath stated that "physical AI" is currently in its "LEGO era," suggesting it is awaiting its "ChatGPT moment" for robotics.

items.title: Figma co-founder Dylan Field thinks MCP is not a perfect protocol
items.summary: Figma co-founder Dylan Field stated that MCP (likely a protocol related to design collaboration) is not a perfect protocol, and Figma aims to support as many standards as possible without exposing all its data.

items.title: Inspired Capital closes $450M fourth fund as New York pushes back on Silicon Valley’s gravitational pull
items.summary: Inspired Capital, a New York-based venture capital firm, has closed its fourth fund at $450 million, signaling New York's growing presence in the tech investment landscape against Silicon Valley's dominance.

items.title: Mamdani says feds have abdicated on AI, urges New Yorkers to push back
items.summary: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani asserted that federal authorities have failed to regulate AI, encouraging New Yorkers to resist narratives of an inevitable AI takeover and demand public-protective regulations.

items.title: Meta’s Muse hits 10M U.S. downloads in 40 days, a milestone reached by only 11 other apps
items.summary: Meta's AI companion app, Muse, has achieved 10 million U.S. downloads within its first 40 days, a milestone reached by only eleven other applications, including Threads. Data also indicates that Muse is exhibiting higher user retention rates compared to its AI competitors.

items.title: Nscale and Anthropic are reportedly in talks for yet another $45B compute deal
items.summary: Anthropic is reportedly in discussions with Nscale for a substantial $45 billion compute deal, marking it as another significant agreement in a series of large compute deals for the company over the past year.

items.title: Otter.ai raises $320 million from General Catalyst’s growth fund for its meeting tool
items.summary: Otter.ai, known for its meeting note-taking tool, secured $320 million from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund to fuel enterprise growth, international expansion, and product innovation without equity dilution.

items.title: Oura adds new fitness metrics to show how workouts impact your body
items.summary: Oura is introducing new fitness metrics to its smart ring, aiming to provide users with a deeper understanding of how workouts affect their bodies. This innovation seeks to differentiate Oura amid increasing competition in the smart ring market.

items.title: Plants can speak using electricity, so this startup built an AI model to decipher their language
items.summary: Electric Plant, a startup, has developed an AI-powered translator to interpret the subtle electrical signals that plants use to communicate. This technology aims to help humans understand the "language" of plants.

items.title: Spotify launches paid podcast memberships with perks beyond bonus content
items.summary: Spotify has introduced new paid podcast memberships, allowing podcasters to offer exclusive perks like ad-free listening, early access, and bonus content while retaining 90% of the revenue.

items.title: Streaming guide JustWatch becomes a streamer itself
items.summary: JustWatch, a popular streaming search guide with 50 million users, is expanding into its own streaming service, offering free ad-supported content, a $3.99/month ad-free tier, and movie rentals.

items.title: TikTok staff raised child safety concerns, but executives reportedly failed to act
items.summary: Court documents indicate that TikTok employees raised concerns about child safety risks on the platform, but executives reportedly did not adequately address these issues. Staff expressed frustration over the response to risks to children.

items.title: Walmart’s Flipkart is quietly building a food delivery challenger in India
items.summary: Walmart-owned Flipkart is reportedly expanding access to its food-delivery service to thousands of employees in India, signaling a quiet build-up before a public launch to challenge existing services.

items.title: Yelp can now call on your behalf to check wait times at a restaurant
items.summary: Yelp is integrating new AI features into its app, including the ability to call restaurants on a user's behalf to check wait times and create personalized recommendations.

items.title: David Sabatini Lost Everything After Being Accused of Sexual Harassment. He Just Won $6 Million.
items.summary: Molecular biologist David Sabatini, who lost his career after being accused of sexual harassment, has won a $6 million defamation lawsuit against his accuser, Kristin Knouse, with the jury rejecting her counterclaims. Sabatini, once a Nobel Prize contender, had faced unemployment and professional ostracization.

items.title: Douglas Murray: France Stares Down the Abyss of History
items.summary: Douglas Murray argues that the current widespread unrest in France, characterized by "apocalyptic" scenes, is being fueled by hardened adult rioters and various activist groups, rather than merely student protests. He suggests identifying the true drivers requires direct observation beyond conventional explanations.

items.title: Inside France’s Night of Terror
items.summary: This article details the "civil war–like scenes" of looting and arson across France during recent protests, including the burning of Limoges city hall. Witnesses describe thousands of masked young people storming shops, leaving residents traumatized by the apocalyptic destruction.

items.title: How to Stop Waiting and Start Living: A Jolt from Henry James
items.summary: Drawing on Henry James's novella "The Beast in the Jungle," this article explores how people can spend their lives in an expectant "near-life existence," waiting for a transformative event instead of truly living. It argues that true failure lies in "not being anything" and highlights how love can be the transformative experience one awaits.

items.title: Adobe Lightroom mobile can now open closed eyes in photos with a simple tap
items.summary: Adobe Lightroom mobile now features a generative AI-powered "Open Eyes Quick Action" that can automatically correct closed eyes in photos with a single tap. This new feature allows users to easily save otherwise great photos by replacing closed eyes, similar to a decade-old Photoshop Elements function.

items.title: AMD is bringing FSR 4.1 to Xbox consoles and handhelds
items.summary: AMD is expanding its FSR 4.1 upscaling technology to Xbox Series S/X consoles, laptops, 6000-series GPUs, and handhelds like the Xbox Ally X. This update, already available for Radeon RX 9000-series cards, can improve performance in over 300 supported games.

items.title: Arturia’s MiniFreak 49 makes its Freak synths more professional
items.summary: Arturia has introduced the MiniFreak 49, a new synthesizer in its Freak line, featuring 49 full-sized, semi-weighted keys and interface improvements. While similar internally to the existing MiniFreak, it offers a more professional form factor with proper pitch and mod wheels.

items.title: Chrome will now show a warning before you visit ‘suspicious’ sites
items.summary: Google Chrome is launching a new safety feature that will display warnings for "suspicious" websites exhibiting qualities associated with phishing, malware, and scams. This builds on an existing two-stage system for flagged file downloads and requires Chrome's Enhanced Protection to be active.

items.title: Spotify pulled 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations
items.summary: Spotify removed over 50 million AI-generated "slop" and spam songs from user recommendations in the past year, also adjusting its system to prioritize human artists. The company noted a decrease in listener complaints about such content, though it hasn't mandated labels for all AI tracks.

items.title: The $20,000 Voxel bot will help you find misplaced things around your home
items.summary: Tuesday Labs has opened reservations for Voxel, a bi-pedal home robot designed to learn and perform routine tasks, including finding misplaced items. The robot, priced around $20,000, features articulated arms and an advanced vision system, with shipping expected in 2028.

items.title: The Gospel according to Peter (Thiel)
items.summary: Silicon Valley is experiencing a new wave of apocalyptic worldviews, with effective altruism (EA) driving concerns about AI-induced doomsday scenarios. This philosophy, popular among AI industry leaders, is contrasted with rival cosmologies from tech titans like Peter Thiel.

items.title: TikTok employees said they knew about child safety issues, but execs failed to act
items.summary: Court records reveal TikTok staffers repeatedly warned executives about child safety risks, including minors bypassing age restrictions and appearing in transactional sexual content, but executives allegedly failed to act. These depositions are part of a multi-district litigation concerning platform harms to children.
